newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia confirms Qantas flight rights.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia confirms Qantas flight rights.

text.p: The International Air Services Commission said on Wednesday it had renewed Qantas Airways Ltd's allocation of services to Indonesia, Malaysia and New Zealand.
The commission said Qantas would be allocated the equivalent of 7.6 Boeing 747 flights per week to Indonesia, 1.8 747 flights per week to Malaysia and an unlimited capacity to New Zealand.
There were no other applicants for the New Zealand capacity, it said.
Qantas is 25 percent owned by British Airways Plc.
The commission is charged with allocating Australian air traffic rights between carriers.
When Australia ended Qantas's monopoly flag-carrier status in 1992, the airline's existing allocations were to last until only mid-1997.
However, the commission's policy is to renew the rights unless someone could show reason for a change.
